subject: Health and Movement Science
name: Health and Movement Science, Year 11
about: HSC, Health for individuals and the body in motion
syllabus: NSW Health and Movement Science 11-12 Syllabus (2023), Year 11 focus areas (replaced PDHPE Stage 6)

points.title: Dimensions of health
points.brief: Health has physical, mental, emotional, social and spiritual dimensions, which affect each other.

points.title: Health as dynamic and subjective
points.brief: A person's health changes over time and how healthy they feel depends on their own values and situation.

points.title: Determinants of health
points.brief: Individual factors, such as knowledge and genetics, sociocultural factors, such as family and culture, socioeconomic factors, such as income and education, and environmental factors, such as access to services.

points.title: Health literacy
points.brief: The skills to find, understand, judge and use health information to make good decisions.

points.title: Health behaviours and risk factors
points.brief: Behaviours such as physical activity, diet, sleep, smoking and alcohol use raise or lower the risk of illness.

points.title: Protective factors and resilience
points.brief: Supportive relationships, a sense of belonging and coping skills help people stay well and recover from setbacks.

points.title: Health promotion
points.brief: Helping people and communities take control of their health, through education, healthy environments and policy.

points.title: The Ottawa Charter
points.brief: The WHO's 1986 framework has five action areas, building healthy public policy, creating supportive environments, strengthening community action, developing personal skills and reorienting health services.

points.title: Principles of social justice in health
points.brief: Equity, diversity and supportive environments guide health promotion so that it reaches people with the greatest need.

points.title: Community health resources
points.brief: Services such as GPs, community health centres, helplines and school counsellors support people's health, but not everyone can reach them easily.

points.title: Young people's health
points.brief: Young Australians' health is shaped by mental health, sexual health, road safety, sleep, social media and substance use, and by where they live.

units.title: The body and mind in motion

points.title: The skeletal system
points.brief: Bones support the body, protect organs and act as levers. Joints, such as hinge and ball-and-socket joints, allow different movements.

points.title: The muscular system
points.brief: Skeletal muscles work in pairs, with an agonist that contracts and an antagonist that relaxes. Contractions can be concentric, eccentric or isometric.

points.title: Muscle fibre types
points.brief: Slow-twitch fibres resist fatigue and suit endurance. Fast-twitch fibres contract quickly and powerfully but tire fast.

points.title: The cardiovascular system
points.brief: The heart pumps blood through arteries, capillaries and veins, carrying oxygen and nutrients to muscles and removing waste.

points.title: The respiratory system
points.brief: Air moves through the airways to the alveoli, where oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

points.title: ATP and energy
points.brief: Muscles run on ATP. The body has only a little stored, so it must keep remaking it through three energy systems.

points.title: The ATP-PC system
points.brief: Gives energy fastest for very short, explosive efforts, such as a sprint start, but runs out in about 10 seconds.

points.title: The anaerobic glycolysis system
points.brief: Breaks down glucose without oxygen for hard efforts of about 10 seconds to two minutes, producing by-products linked to fatigue.

points.title: The aerobic system
points.brief: Uses oxygen to break down carbohydrates and fats for long, steady activity. It is slow to start but lasts for hours.

points.title: Energy systems working together
points.brief: All three systems work at once, and the intensity and length of the activity decide which one supplies most of the energy.

points.title: Motion
points.brief: Linear motion is in a straight line, angular motion turns around an axis, and general motion combines the two.

points.title: Balance and stability
points.brief: A wider base, a lower centre of gravity and keeping the line of gravity over the base all make a body more stable.

points.title: Force and levers
points.brief: Muscles pull on bones, which act as levers to produce movement. Applying force over a longer time or distance gives more speed.

points.title: Stages of skill acquisition
points.brief: Learners move from the cognitive stage, thinking about each step, to the associative stage, refining it, to the autonomous stage, where it is automatic.

points.title: Feedback in learning skills
points.brief: Feedback can be internal or external, and can describe the result (knowledge of results) or the movement itself (knowledge of performance).

points.title: Motivation and arousal
points.brief: Intrinsic motivation comes from enjoyment, extrinsic from rewards. Performance is best at a moderate level of arousal, and anxiety can harm it.

points.title: Framing a research question
points.brief: A clear question about health or movement that a group can test with data, such as whether a warm-up changes sprint times.

points.title: Collecting data
points.brief: Choosing valid methods, such as surveys, fitness tests or observations, and recording results carefully.

points.title: Working as a team
points.brief: Sharing roles, communicating clearly and reflecting on how the group worked together are part of the investigation.

points.title: Research ethics
points.brief: Participants must give informed consent, be kept safe and have their information kept private.
